Forage, fletching, and things that fix you. Mostly the first two. Have a look.
The Hollow Log. Hollow log, soft moss, warm stew. Seventy gold, and I'll even let you choose which log.
the Hollow Log
The soldiers came a month back. Fifty of them, white and gold, the Hierophant's sun on every shield.
The big one with the beard didn't even go in. Sat on my woodpile eating our apples while his men carried the Keeper's light out in a box.
Didn't pay for the apples, either.
You've seen her? Truly? Is she— is she very old?
Of course she is. I only meant — is she very _kind_? I always imagined she was.
I'm writing an epic about Keeper Elowen. Nobody in Rootholm has seen her in thirty years.
Some say she is four hundred years old. Some say she has turned into a tree. I have rhymed both possibilities, just in case.
I'm not allowed in the Tangle anymore. Or near the Tangle. Or near anyone who's been near the Tangle.
Mum's very thorough.
I tied a ribbon for Gran on the Memory Tree. A yellow one. She liked yellow.
The pretty lights in the forest weren't her. Ilse said. Ilse says it's all right to miss her anyway.
When I'm sixteen I'm going to be a Warden like the big one. Or a Rogue like the small one.
He said I could be both. He said that's allowed now. Is that allowed now?
The Memory Tree
Fern's crates: bundles of arrows fletched with jay feathers, jars of honey, a sign reading NO HAGGLING, and under it, smaller: (a little haggling).
A statue of a Keeper, so old that her face has worn smooth. Somebody — recently — has put a crown of daisies on her head.
The Lantern
The Lantern of Thornwood. Roots have climbed it to the gallery; blossom grows inside the lamp-glass.
The cradle at its heart is empty. A bird has started a nest in it.
The trees here grow too close to pass. For now.
